newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes up in late fillip.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes up in late fillip.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed up 90 basis points at 29.50 percent in a late surge after a session that was mostly determined by the changing fortunes of the peso, traders said.
"The overnight rate returned to opening levels, probably because some dealers were desperate to get rid of paper at any price before the close," said a trader.

Overnight rates had opened 95 basis points up at 29.55 percent, in response to an early slide in the peso. The peso then recovered to close slightly firmer, and the Cetes rate fell back to a session low of 28.50 percent.
"As long as the peso continues to ebb and flow, secondary interest rates will do the same," a dealer said.
Other traders meanwhile expected secondary rates to trend downwards for the rest of the week, especially if October inflation figures due out on Thursday turned out to be favorable.
A Reuters survey of ten analysts in Mexico City showed an average forecast of 1.31 percent for October inflation MXAAP, compared to 1.60 percent in September.
Banco de Mexico earlier injected 3.179 billion pesos into the market by auctioning two credits at 31.44 and 31.15 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 125 basis points at 31.25 percent.
Total credit maturities expected for Thursday were 2.00 billion pesos, and ensuing liquidity shortages could be heightened by an overplacement of 253 million pesos from Tuesday's primary auction.
